synthesis.naming_consistency: Generally coherent and descriptive, following a '[Component] [Function] [Type]' pattern, but inconsistently mixes source code modules with documentation, research notes, and build scripts without a clear naming convention to distinguish artifact types.
synthesis.architectural_layering: No explicit architectural layers are defined in the metadata (all arrays are empty). While a logical hierarchy is implied (Hardware Transport → Gesture Abstraction → Domain Controllers → UI/Shell → Build/Release), the dependency graph forms a flat star topology centered on 'core-orchestration' rather than strict layered boundaries, indicating tight coupling and a lack of enforced architectural stratification.
redundancy_flags: Release/Sparkle pipeline fragmentation: clusters 18, 20, 21, 22, and 23 all cover overlapping signing, appcast, and packaging concerns across XML, templates, docs, and shell scripts.

Research vs. Implementation duplication: Audio (clusters 14 & 15) and Display (clusters 3 & 19) each split functionality between a working controller and a standalone research/fallback strategy document.
MIDI boundary ambiguity: Virtual endpoint (cluster 7) and action mapping engine (cluster 4) both handle MIDI generation without a clearly defined protocol boundary.
synthesis.key_insight: The system exhibits a research-driven, star-topology architecture where nearly every subsystem bypasses intermediate layers to depend directly on a central orchestration hub and the AppDelegate. This flat structure is mirrored by significant fragmentation in the release pipeline and a recurring pattern of pairing implementation files with standalone research documents, indicating the codebase is functionally capable but architecturally unlayered, heavily reliant on manual processes, and ripe for consolidation, explicit boundary enforcement, and automated CI/CD integration.
